passage:
Tuesday night, hostel.
Zainab talked to me for two hours on the steps behind the library. She hasn't been to lectures in three weeks. She said she lies awake till four and then can't get up, and that her family thinks she's topping the class. "Don't tell anyone, Yusuf. Please."
I'm so torn. She trusted me, and I don't want to be the one who ruins that. But I can't stop thinking about her face when she said, "I'm so tired of everything." I'm angry too, honestly, at how much pressure she's under.
I asked her straight out if she felt safe. She said yes, just exhausted. So I asked her to see the college counsellor, and said I'd walk her there. She said, "Tomorrow, 11." We agreed she'd call me or the warden tonight if it gets worse. At midnight I knocked; she answered and said she was going to sleep. I've set an alarm.

qa.q: How long has Zainab been missing lectures?
qa.a: She hasn't been to lectures in three weeks.

qa.q: What is Yusuf torn between, and what worries Yusuf most?
qa.a: Yusuf is torn between loyalty to Zainab's trust and worry, especially about her saying "I'm so tired of everything", and also feels angry about the pressure on her.

qa.q: Which steps did Yusuf take that were wise?
qa.a: Yusuf asked directly whether she felt safe, agreed she would call Yusuf or the warden that night if things got worse, checked on her at midnight, and offered to walk her to the college counsellor at a set time.

qa.q: What might it mean to Zainab that Yusuf will walk with her?
qa.a: She may feel less alone and more able to face the counsellor, since carrying it by herself had become exhausting.

grounding: A young adult entrusted with Zainab's troubles feels torn between loyalty and worry, and urges Zainab to get qualified help instead of carrying it alone.

passage:
Afreen: can I tell you something if you promise not to tell anyone
Usha: you can tell me anything
Afreen: I don't think I can do this anymore. everyone would be better off
Usha: Afreen, are you thinking of hurting yourself?
Afreen: I don't know. maybe. please don't tell anyone
Usha: I care about you too much to keep this one. are you safe right now? where are you?
Afreen: room
Usha: calling you now. pick up
(missed call)
Usha: I'm calling your warden and I'm on my way over. stay on the phone with me
Afreen: ok
(twenty minutes later)
Usha: the warden's with you now and the counsellor is coming. I'm 5 minutes away. I'm not going anywhere
Afreen: ok. thank you

qa.q: Where did Afreen say they were right now?
What was Usha feeling when Afreen asked not to tell anyone, and what shows it?
qa.a: Usha was deeply worried but clear, writing "I care about you too much to keep this one" and acting at once.

qa.q: Which steps by Usha kept Afreen safer?
qa.a: Usha asked directly about self-harm, checked where Afreen was, called the warden, stayed on the phone and went over straight away.

qa.q: What might it be like for Afreen when the warden arrives?
qa.a: Afreen may feel scared or exposed, but also less alone, knowing people came quickly because they care.

grounding: A young adult told of Afreen's serious distress refuses to carry it alone and brings in the warden and a counsellor at once.
